title: Eastern Plaguelands
body: Before the plague these hills were the Eastweald, governed from Stratholme, the second city of Lordaeron. Here Prince Arthas put Stratholme to the sword rather than let its plagued people rise, and here the Scourge made its deepest home. Rot runs through the woods, and towns like Darrowshire and Northdale belong to the dead. The living hold on where they can: the Argent Dawn at Light's Hope Chapel, the Scarlet Crusade at Tyr's Hand.

parts.body: In the war against the Lich King the Scourge has turned its strength north to Northrend, and above the hills near Light's Hope now floats Acherus, the Ebon Hold of the death knights.

title: Darrowshire
body: Darrowshire, named for Darrowmere Lake to its west, was a village of humble, hardworking folk in the southern foothills until the Scourge came. Its militia, a company of troops and paladins of the Silver Hand stood against the ghoul lord Horgus and the death knight Marduk the Black, and the village did not survive the night. In one house the ghost of a little girl still waits for her father.

title: Corin's Crossing
body: Corin's Crossing grew up where the roads met between Andorhal, Darrowshire, Stratholme and Tyr's Hand. The Scourge holds it now: dark casters and summoners of the Cult of the Damned work among ghouls and stitched horrors, and many of those ghouls were once the good folk of Darrowshire, still bound in their rotting bodies.

title: The Infectis and Pestilent Scars
body: Two great wounds cut the land near Corin's Crossing. The Infectis Scar was made by dark magic: when the rune-laden sword of Marduk the Black shattered on a dwarf's shield, the blade sank into the earth and ate out the gorge, and its pieces lie at the bottom still. The Pestilent Scar is a natural rift, but the plague has found it all the same.

title: Tyr's Hand
body: Tyr's Hand, a walled city in the southeast named for an ancient keeper, is one of the oldest holy sites of the Church of the Light. The Scarlet Crusade rules it now as its stronghold in the east, with the Scarlet Basilica at its heart. Crusader Lord Valdelmar commands within, High General Abbendis close at hand, and each day a courier rides in from the Crusade's command in Stratholme.

title: Light's Hope Chapel
body: Light's Hope Chapel is among the oldest holy sites of the Eastweald, and the heroes of Lordaeron lie in the catacombs beneath it. The Argent Dawn has made it the headquarters of its war on the Scourge under Lord Maxwell Tyrosus, a veteran who fought beside Uther, and Horde and Alliance alike are welcome. Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff hands out the Dawn's commission and pays for the scourgestones brought back from the field.

parts.body: As the Scourge stirs against the wider world, envoys of the Cenarion Circle, the Earthen Ring and even the Scarlet Crusade have come to sit beside the Dawn's own Brotherhood of the Light.

Leonid Barthalomew, one of the Dawn's most revered, is undead. He died in the Scourging of Lordaeron, was freed by the Banshee Queen and chose the Dawn over the Forsaken, treating his undeath as a weapon against the Scourge.

title: Zul'Mashar
body: Zul'Mashar in the far northeast is the capital of the Mossflayers, a small tribe of forest trolls worn down by long wars with the humans of Lordaeron. The plague has found them too. Shadowhunters, scouts and cannibals crowd the ruins under Warlord Thresh'jin, and above them rises the ziggurat of Mazra'Alor.

parts.body: A torn scroll tells how the plague reached them: a band of Mossflayers ate tainted meat on the road, and one of them, Hameya, began to hear a lich urging him to infect his people.

title: Quel'Lithien Lodge
body: Near the road to Quel'Thalas stands Quel'Lithien Lodge, a hunting lodge of the high elves that once hosted Farstrider rangers. Rangers and pathstriders keep it still under Ranger Lord Hawkspear, friendly to the Alliance and quick to draw on the Horde. Nearby the priestess Aurora Skycaller grieves that her people are as shattered as any broken relic.

title: The Watchtowers
body: Four old towers of Lordaeron stand over the Eastern Plaguelands: Crown Guard Tower in the south, Eastwall Tower in the east, Northpass Tower near the road north and Plaguewood Tower at the edge of the blighted forest. All were left empty when the kingdom fell, and their banners still hang, waiting for someone to claim them.

parts.body: The towers will not stay empty. The Alliance means to seize them and tighten a noose around the Forsaken lands to the west, and the Horde fights to drive it out.

title: Plaguewood
body: The Plaguewood south of Stratholme is the most diseased corner of a diseased land, a fair woodland that Prince Arthas crossed on his road to the city and that the blight has since swollen with giant mushrooms and rot. Ziggurats and slaughterhouses rise among the trees. At its western edge lies Terrordale, a ghost town whose one merchant never left the inn.

parts.body: Above the forest hangs the necropolis Naxxramas, the floating citadel of Kel'Thuzad and the seat of his power in the Plaguelands.
Since the Scourge began to strike at the wider world, the Argent Dawn has held the way into the necropolis, and it lets in only those it judges worthy.
The fighting has moved on. The Scourge has turned its strength north to Northrend, and the necropolis is gone from the sky, though the ziggurats still stand among the trees.

title: Stratholme
body: Stratholme was the second city of Lordaeron. When the plague reached it in tainted grain, Prince Arthas ordered its people put to death before they could rise, and the city burned; many chose the flames over becoming Scourge, and their spirits still walk its streets. Today Baron Rivendare holds most of the city for Kel'Thuzad, while the Scarlet Crusade has walled itself into the Scarlet Bastion.

title: Nathanos Blightcaller
body: In life Nathanos Marris was a ranger lord of Lordaeron, trained by the high elves to a rank no other human had held. The Scourge overran his family's farm, the Marris Stead, and he rose in undeath; now, as Nathanos Blightcaller, he is one of the first champions of the Banshee Queen. He keeps the stead with his blighthounds and trains her recruits with open contempt.

parts.body: A registry at Quel'Lithien Lodge records his mortal life. He wants it back badly enough to send killers for it, and forbids them to read a word of it.

title: Pamela Redpath
body: Pamela Redpath was a little girl when the Scourge came to Darrowshire. Her aunt hid her in the family home and told her to stay put while her father went to fight, and her ghost has stayed ever since. She does not understand what happened. She waits for her daddy, the bravest man in the whole world, and wants her doll, lost somewhere in town.

parts.body: Her aunt Marlene still haunts the family's house on the hill south of Andorhal, and her uncle Carlin serves the Argent Dawn at Light's Hope; at night Pamela can hear him crying.
sources: quest 5149 description (auntie told me to stay; father had to fight; bad people whisper; doll)

parts.body: She had a big sister too. Jessica fled Lordaeron before the Scourge swept through it, and she lives still, far away in Winterspring.
sources: quest 5149 description (auntie told me to stay; father had to fight; bad people whisper; doll)

parts.body: Her long wait is over. When the battle was fought again and her father's spirit saved, he came home to her at last, and she made tea for the one who saved him.
